To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we directly measured the S-branch R-branch rotational coherence lifetimes of carbon dioxide and nitrogen, and we showed that these measurements are different from previous measurements.
direct measurements of collisionally induced broadening of rotational Raman lines of CO(2)-S branch (ΔJ = 2) transitions differ from previous measurements and theory by 7%–25%.

we measured the S-branch collisional linewidth broadened coefficients of CO(2)-X for J = 0 to 52 and that the broadened linewidth coefficients of the CO(2)-Ar system agree with previous measurements and theoretical calculations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel technique to measure directly the collisionally broadened linewidths of S-branch transitions of CO( 2) and the associated Raman coherence lifetime.

understanding the collisional broadening mechanism of S-branch rotational Raman transitions in the gas phase and with improving the accuracy of the collisional-broadening coefficients for CO(2) in the S-branch transitions, which are important to the accurate modeling of the Earth's atmosphere.
the development of new techniques for the detection of chemical species, and the development of new laser sources for applications in medicine and the military.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the direct measurements of the collisionally broadened S-branch RCO(2) linewidths of CO(2), when converted to broadening coefficients, are in excellent agreement with the theoretical calculations and the frequency-domain rotational RCO(2)-linewidth measurements of CO(2).

the direct measurements of collisionally induced S-branch R-branch Raman linewidths are in good agreement with the previously reported values for both the CO(2)-He and CO(2) -N(2) systems, but the CO(2) self-broadening coefficients are larger than those reported previously.
the direct measurement results are more reliable than the frequency-domain measurement results and theoretical calculations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the collisionally broadened S-branch linewidths are larger than the previously reported values, but smaller than the theoretical predictions.
the Raman linewidths are narrower than the infrared linewidths.
the collisionally broadened rotational Raman linewidths are smaller than the previously reported linewidths.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the collisional broadening coefficients of the S-branch transitions of CO( 2) can be determined directly from time-domain experiments.

the collisionally broadened rotational linewidths of CO(2), which are of fundamental importance in the study of atmospheric chemistry and in the development of laser-based spectroscopic sensors, are not well known and should be measured directly.
the Raman linewidths are significantly larger than the infrared linewidths for the S-branch transitions of CO( 2) and that the broadening coefficients of CO(2)-S(0) are smaller than those of CO(2).
